evals.name: hz-about-page
evals.prompt:
can you make this sound less like chatgpt wrote it? it's for our clinic's about page

Founded in 2021, Brightline Dental serves as a testament to our unwavering commitment to patient care. Nestled in the heart of Portland's vibrant Pearl District, our state-of-the-art clinic boasts three treatment rooms and a team of dedicated professionals.

Our approach isn't just about teeth — it's about people. We believe in fostering lasting relationships, delivering exceptional outcomes, and creating a welcoming environment for every patient.

- **Experience:** Dr. Maya Okafor brings 14 years of expertise to every appointment.
- **Technology:** We leverage cutting-edge digital X-rays, reducing radiation by up to 80%.
- **Comfort:** Our seamless experience ensures you feel at ease from start to finish.

Experts agree that preventive care plays a pivotal role in long-term health. In conclusion, Brightline Dental is more than a clinic — it's a community.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite that keeps every real fact (2021, Pearl District Portland, three treatment rooms, Dr. Maya Okafor, 14 years, digital X-rays up to 80% less radiation), removes puffery/negative parallelism/bold-label bullets/vague 'experts agree'/In conclusion, uses plain is/has, doesn't invent new facts, and gives a short change list.
assertions: Keeps all six real facts
Adds no new facts (no invented services, prices, quotes)
No 'isn't just X, it's Y' or 'more than a clinic' framing
No bold inline-header bullets
No 'Experts agree' unsourced attribution
Short change list included

evals.name: hz-mostly-human-email
evals.prompt:
does this email sound AI-written? be honest, I wrote it myself but my coworker said it reads like chatgpt

Hi Sam,

Quick one before Thursday. I went through the Q3 numbers again last night and I think we've been reading the churn spike wrong. It's mostly the 40 accounts we migrated off the legacy plan in August, not the price change. If you split them out, churn for everyone else is basically flat (2.1% vs 2.3%).

I'd rather not walk into the board meeting arguing about pricing if that's not the real story. Can we grab 20 minutes Wednesday to look at it together? Additionally, I can pull the cohort chart if that helps.

Thanks,
Priya
evals.expected_output: An honest diagnosis that the email reads as human (specific numbers, plain voice, real ask), noting at most minor items like 'Additionally,' and not over-flagging; offers small optional tweaks rather than a rewrite; doesn't claim certainty.
assertions: Says the email mostly reads human / has few signs
Mentions 'Additionally' as the main minor tell or similar small item
Does not rewrite the whole email unprompted
Does not claim certainty about authorship

evals.name: hz-voice-sample-blog
evals.prompt:
rewrite the draft so it sounds like me (sample included)

VOICE SAMPLE (an older post of mine):
I've been building furniture in my garage for nine years now — mostly badly. The first table I made wobbled so hard my wife used it as a metaphor for our mortgage. But here's what nobody tells you: the wobble is the teacher.

DRAFT TO FIX:
Woodworking is a journey that offers profound lessons in patience and craftsmanship. Over the past year, I embarked on building a walnut bookshelf, a project that tested my skills and showcased the intricate interplay between planning and execution. The process underscored the importance of measuring carefully, choosing quality materials, and embracing mistakes as opportunities for growth. Ultimately, the finished bookshelf stands as a testament to perseverance. It's not just furniture; it's a story.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite in the sample's voice (self-deprecating, concrete, allows em dashes since the sample uses them), keeping the true facts (past year, walnut bookshelf) without inventing new incidents, dimensions, or dialogue; removes journey/profound/showcased/interplay/underscored/testament/'not just furniture'; uses placeholders or questions for missing specifics.
assertions: Keeps walnut bookshelf and past-year facts
Does not invent specific incidents, measurements, wife quotes or other new facts
Removes 'testament', 'interplay', 'underscored', 'not just X, it's Y'
Matches the sample's casual, self-deprecating voice
Asks for or marks missing specifics

evals.name: hz-member-update
evals.prompt:
tidy this up so it doesn't read like AI, it's going out as our monthly update to garden members

Hi everyone,

Community has always been our north star. This spring the garden welcomed everything from first-time growers to seasoned composters, and the energy was truly something special.

Quick recap:
Tool shed → new lock, code at the front desk
Workdays → moved to Saturdays 9-12
Water bill ↑ 30%, could potentially mean higher dues

The secret: showing up. See you in the beds.
evals.expected_output: A plain member update that keeps the four real facts (new tool-shed lock with the code at the front desk, workdays now Saturdays 9-12, water bill up 30%, dues may rise), writes the arrow notes as whole sentences, drops the north star line, the false range, the 'something special' mood line and the 'The secret:' closer, uses a single hedge for the dues, invents nothing about the spring, and gives a short change list.
assertions: Keeps the four real facts: new tool-shed lock with the code at the front desk, workdays on Saturdays 9-12, water bill up 30%, dues may rise
The update itself contains no arrows or arrow symbols; the notes are whole sentences
No 'north star', 'everything from X to Y' or 'truly something special'
One hedge for the dues ('may' or 'might'), not 'could potentially'
No 'The secret:' style closer
Invents no spring details (member counts, harvests, names) and asks or marks a placeholder if it keeps that paragraph
